text:
Anya: Quick design check — ran into an edge where two rules get assigned identical priority and the editor currently just shows both in a stack. Proposal: show a compact 'conflict' chip next to the top rule with a Resolve button that opens a small modal with a side-by-side diff and a quick action to 'Promote / Demote / Merge'. Mike: I like the chip idea. two quick Qs: does Resolve block the main flow? can it be keyboard-only? Anya: The modal should not block — light dismissible, focus returns to the rule list. Keyboard-first: open with Enter on the chip and arrow-focus inside the diff. Josie: Accessibility nits: make the chip accessible to screen readers (role=button) and announce the conflict via aria-live when it appears. Also need clear copy for what "Merge" actually does. Samir: From preview/simulation POV we need this to reflect in the sandbox immediately. If a user merges rules in the modal, the sim traffic should re-run for that route only. Avoid a full-sim run. Lexi: Copy suggestion for the chip: "Conflict (2 rules)". Modal header: "Resolve priority conflict". Buttons: "Promote to priority X", "Demote to priority Y", "Merge rules" (with tooltip explaining merge — picks union of selectors, rule text is concatenated). Mike: Small UX worry: too many CTAs in modal. Maybe prioritize Promote/Demote and hide Merge under "More actions"? Anya: Good call. Keep primary CTA to resolve ordering (Promote/Demote). Merge is secondary and requires confirmation. Josie: Example live region snippet I can add to the accessibility checklist:```
Priority conflict detected between "Payment - USD" and "Payment - EUR"
```That announces when a conflict is created via paste/import or programmatic change. Samir: Implementation notes: we should wire the modal actions to the preview engine via the same route API used by the sim UI. Quick patch: API call PATCH /routes/:id/resolve-conflict with body {action: "promote", target_priority: 10}. Response returns updated route delta which the sim can apply incrementally. Lexi: UX microcopy: toast vs inline — when a conflict is auto-detected on import, do we show an ephemeral toast + highlight the items, or create the chip inline and expand it? I vote for both: toast to notify + inline chip to persist until resolved. Mike: +1 for toast+chip. For the toast text: "Priority conflict detected in Route: Checkout — Click to review." Make the toast link to focus the top conflicting rule. Anya: Interaction edgecase: what if two conflicts cascade (A vs B and B vs C)? Do we show one chip per conflict or group them? I propose grouping by affected rule: each rule shows chips for conflicts with immediate neighbors, with the modal able to navigate through related conflicts. Josie: Accessibility followups: when toast shows, ensure it is reachable via keyboard and appears in the toast list in the top-right (not just transient). Also add a visible focus ring on the chip and aria-describedby linking to the conflict summary. design-bot: Uploaded mock: https://redwood.design/mockups/conflict-chip-1711234567.png — shows chip, modal, and sim toggle states. :sparkles: Samir: Dev checklist draft: 1) announce conflict via aria-live 2) render conflict chip (button) 3) open keyboard-accessible modal with diffs 4) call /resolve-conflict API 5) trigger incremental sim only for affected route 6) surface secondary action "Merge" behind confirmation 7) add unit tests for focus/keyboard flows. Lexi: Also add copy unit tests for pluralization: "1 conflict" vs "2 conflicts" and ensure screen-reader phrasing reads natural language. Anya: Cool. Next steps: Josie will add aria snippets and copy. Samir will spec the incremental sim API. Mike & I will prototype the modal interactions and run it in the next UX sync. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
